subject: Kite.ai POC performance plan and cost paths

From: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
To: Emma Li <emma@kite.ai>, Kite AI Eng <eng@kite.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>

Subject: Kite.ai POC performance discovery — post-call notes & immediate asks

Hi Emma / Kite team,

Thanks again for taking the time today — solid discussion. Quick recap and the asks we promised:

Summary of SLOs you asked us to qualify
- Latency: p95 <= 250ms for payloads up to 512 tokens (end-to-end generation).
- Throughput: sustained 120 req/sec for the primary endpoint (burst to 200 req/sec).
- Concurrency: target steady-state concurrency ~= 40 concurrent requests; spikes to 100 for 30s allowed.
- Streaming: streaming output required for the chat endpoint; first token ideally < 80ms p50 and subsequent token gaps < 20ms on average.

Sample traffic notes from the call
- Average response length: ~200 tokens; peak responses up to ~1,200 tokens (very rare).
- Typical input sequence length: 40–120 tokens, but multi-turn chat includes a 1–2k token conversation history in some flows.

Immediate asks (action items for Kite)
1) Share 48 hours of representative production traffic (anonymized payloads) or a 24-hour sample with 10% of peak burst patterns. Attach as .json preferred.
2) Confirm whether streaming must be server-sent-chunks or if client can accept short-poll partial results.
3) Provide a test account/API key for Redwood perf harness (read-only) so we can run an initial synthetic replay.

What Redwood will deliver next (timeline)
- Day 0–3: Replay baseline against our hosted runner (no quantization) to validate p95 baseline.
- Day 4–7: Run three candidate configurations: (A) latency-first (higher-cost GPU + smaller model variant), (B) throughput-first (continuous batching + higher concurrency), (C) hybrid with model-variant routing + prefix caching. We will return per-config p95/p50, token cost, and recommended quantization profile.

High-level cost levers we intend to evaluate
- Continuous batching: batching window tuned to 40–120ms depending on burstiness — expect 25–60% token-cost improvement for throughput cases.
- Prefix/KV caching: for repeated conversation prefixes, expect 20–45% reduction in compute.
- Quantization profiles: FP16 -> int8/4-bit experiments; tradeoff matrix will show quality delta vs token-cost.
- Model variants & routing: fallback to smaller model for low-importance queries, route heavy-context requests to larger model.

Attachments: call-recording-20270816.mp3 (audio) attached; we will upload the perf harness instructions to the Drive link below.

Next steps: Emma to share payloads + test key; Redwood (Rishi + team) to schedule replay. Can you share the payloads by EOD Wed (8/18)?

Thanks,
Sean
Sean Gallagher
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

- Conversation history: only ~10% of traffic includes >1k token history; most are single-turn or short context.

Subject: RE: Kite.ai POC performance discovery — quick technical plan and rough cost math

Looping in the technical plan based on the traffic Emma shared. High level — three candidate paths with rough cost and risk sketches.

Assumptions used for back-of-envelope
- Baseline model = LlamaX-13B equivalent run in FP16 on A100-class instances.
- Token counts from Kite payloads and 1M-request per month baseline for normalized cost comparisons.

Option A — Latency-first (p95 <= 250ms)- Setup: dedicate 2x high-clock GPU nodes, smaller optimized model variant (13B quantized to FP16), aggressive routing to minimize batching.- Expected perf: p95 ~220–260ms for 512 tokens depending on burst distribution; streaming first-byte p50 << 80ms.- Cost: ~ $7,800 / 1M requests (model+infra+network), quality high; limited ability to scale to huge sustained throughput without additional nodes.

Option B — Throughput-first (sustained 120 req/s)
- Setup: shared pool with continuous batching (batch window tuned ~80ms), prefix KV cache enabled for repeated contexts, int8 quantization candidate.
- Expected perf: p95 280–400ms for 512 tokens (higher batching latency tail), token-cost reduction 35–55%.
- Cost: ~ $3,900 / 1M requests; better horizontal scaling and cheaper per-token but higher p95 tail during spikes.

Option C — Hybrid model-variant routing + cache- Setup: route low-cost queries to a 7B quantized family, reserve 13B for heavy-context or high-quality responses; use prefix cache + short warm-up kernel for long histories.- Expected perf: mixed — p95 for low-cost queries ~160–200ms; for heavy-context requests ~240–320ms.
- Cost: ~ $4,800 / 1M requests; complexity higher (routing & cache miss handling), but best overall unit economics while protecting latency on common paths.

Streaming requirements
- Websocket-based chunking works best with continuous KV cache; ensure we keep KV cache in-memory per user session to avoid re-serve cost.
- For streaming-first-byte targets, prioritize lower-latency nodes + small early-layer kernels; that pushes to Option A or hybrid with reserved capacity on the streaming path.

Quantization notes & quality checks
- 8-bit quantization (dynamic) looks promising for mid/short responses; for long-history/high-fidelity we recommend FP16 or 4-bit with per-task eval sets.
- We will run automated eval across Kite's sample prompt set and return a delta table (BLEU/semantic-sim) vs baseline.

Concrete next steps (owners & timing)
- Rishi: schedule perf replay against hosted runner (needs API key + sample payloads) — ETA: start Wed 8/18, 48h run.
- Ben: prepare mutual-action plan + cost estimate for commercial offer (shared PM/finance).
- Marissa: coordinate canary schedule with Kite engineers for the streaming endpoint.
- Emma/Kite: share read-only key + confirm websocket vs short-poll preference.

I'll produce a concise report with p50/p95, token cost, and recommended config after the runs (expected by 8/25).

-Rishi
